subject: Water not recgnized correctly by atomtypes in Antechamber

messages.author: Husak Michal
messages.body:
I see water atoms are recognized by atomtypes in Antechamber (gaff and gaff2)
as:
ho-oh-ho
Insted of correct
hw-ow-hw
I see in the ATOMDEF files ow is not defined at all for gaff and gaff2
and I feel hw is incorrectly defined so ho takes priority ...
I can probably fix this definition myself, but it should be fixed in future ....
Help with fixing from experts will be apreciated anyway ...
Related question:
Did anybody try to modify the antechamber atom and bonds definition files
for some other force fields (Dreiding, UFF, MMFF96) ?
Michal Husak
UCT Prague, assoc. professor

messages.author: Carlos Simmerling
messages.body:
I would not use gaff for the water, instead use a well defined and tested
water model. Gaff is intended for molecules without existing models.

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Sun, Sep 22, 2024, Husak Michal via AMBER wrote:
>I see water atoms are recognized by atomtypes in Antechamber (gaff and gaff2)
>as:
>ho-oh-ho
>Insted of correct
>hw-ow-hw
The notion of "correct" atom types is tricky: atom types are only internal
to Amber, and Junmei Wang chose oh/ho. There is nothing wrong with that
choice. It is probably better to use an more standard model for water. All
of Amber's "standard" water models use OW/HW. (Note that atom types are
case-sensitive, so OW/HW is not the same as ow/hw; if there is a problem
with ow/hw definitions in gaff2.dat, then the simplest thing is not to use
those atom types.)
....good luck...dac
p.s. cc-ing to Junemi, he case he wants to look at ow/hw entries in
gaff2.dat.
